title_en: Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua v. Hefei Jianxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over payment of warranty liability for defects
ruling_gist_en: When selling a house that is under a lease, the seller shall inform the buyer of the content of the house lease contract, but the lessee's ability to perform falls within the scope of commercial risk, and does not constitute a pre-contractual obligation of the seller; the buyer shall conduct its own review and bear such risk. When the property title changes during the lease term, unless the parties have otherwise agreed, the rent belongs to the buyer from the date of the title change. After the title change, if the buyer finds it difficult to collect the rent and demands the seller to bear the loss of rent on the grounds that the seller had pre-contractual fault or delivered the house with defects, the people's court shall not support such claim.

full_text_en:
Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua v. Hefei Jianxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over liability for guarantee against defects in performance

Ruling Summary

When a property under lease is sold, the seller shall inform the buyer of the content of the lease contract. However, the lessee's performance capability falls within the scope of commercial risk and does not constitute a pre-contractual obligation of the seller; the buyer shall independently assess and bear such risk. Where the ownership of the property is transferred during the lease term, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the rent shall belong to the buyer as of the date of the ownership transfer. If the buyer, after the ownership transfer, is unable to collect the rent due to difficulties and claims that the seller should bear the rent loss on the grounds of culpa in contrahendo or defects in the delivery of the property, the people's court shall not support such claim.

Plaintiff: Tang Xuefu, male, 51 years old, residing in Xuhui District, Shanghai.

Plaintiff: Pang Hua, female, 46 years old, spouse of Tang Xuefu, residing at the same address as above.

Defendant: Hefei Jianxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dongliu Road, Wanghu Subdistrict, Baohe District, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Rongpu, General Manager of the Company.

The plaintiffs, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, filed a lawsuit with the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, against the defendant, Hefei Jianxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hefei Jianxin Company), concerning a dispute over liability for guarantee against defects in performance.

Plaintiffs' Allegations:

Both the defendant, Hefei Jianxin Company, and Shanghai Greenfield Construction Co., Ltd. Hefei Branch (hereinafter referred to as Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch) are subsidiaries of Shanghai Greenfield Group. Because Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch owed the plaintiff Tang Xuefu a substantial amount of project funds that remained unpaid, and upon arrangement by Shanghai Greenfield Group, the plaintiff Tang Xuefu, Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch, and the defendant, on July 2012, entered into a "Supplementary Agreement on Debt Settlement through Property" regarding the project funds owed by Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch to the plaintiff Tang Xuefu. The agreement stipulated that Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch would purchase properties developed by the defendant, located at Units 113-118, 213-217, 313-317, 413-415, and 417, Block B, Haidun Mansion Commercial Street, Taihu Road, Hefei, and transfer them to the two plaintiffs, with the purchase price to be offset against the project funds payable by the defendant to Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch. On March 29, 2013, the two plaintiffs and the defendant signed fifteen "Commercial Housing Sale Contracts," under which the defendant agreed to sell the properties in question to the two plaintiffs. At the same time, the defendant informed the plaintiffs that the properties were subject to a ten-year lease and requested the plaintiffs to confirm that the original lease contract remained valid. The plaintiffs therefore noted on the supplementary agreement column of the contract: "The client has been informed that the property has been leased and agrees that the original lease shall remain in effect." Subsequently, the plaintiffs repeatedly requested the defendant to handle the procedures for the transfer of rights and obligations under the original lease contract, but the defendant delayed on various grounds. Under the plaintiffs' continuous urging, the defendant promised to collect the rent on their behalf and then pay it to the plaintiffs, and actually transferred RMB 1,258,712 to the plaintiffs as rent for the period from August 1, 2012, to March 31, 2013. On June 4, 2013, the plaintiffs and the defendant completed the procedures for the transfer of property ownership. Thereafter, because the plaintiffs did not receive the rent that the defendant had promised to transfer, Tang Xuefu repeatedly visited the defendant to request assistance in resolving the lease contract and rent collection, but to no avail. Tang Xuefu then went to the leased premises to demand rent from the lessee, Hefei Junyue Enterprise Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hefei Junyue Company), who refused on the grounds that the plaintiff was not a party to the contract and that the rent dispute was pending in court. At that time, the plaintiffs learned that when the parties reached the intention to settle debts through property, Hefei Junyue Company had already begun to default on rent. The defendant, by advancing rent on behalf of the lessee, concealed the significant risks existing in the property being sold in order to facilitate the transaction. After the plaintiffs registered the property ownership, the defendant sued Hefei Junyue Company in court regarding the rent it had advanced and applied for preservation of the equipment in Hefei Junyue Company's business premises, rendering the plaintiffs unable to actually use the property. The plaintiffs requested the court to order: 1. The defendant to compensate the two plaintiffs for rent losses of RMB 5,503,244.84 and corresponding interest losses (the rent loss being the uncollected rent from April 1, 2013, to October 11, 2015; the corresponding interest losses to be calculated on a periodic basis, using the overdue rent as the base, from the date it became due to the date of actual payment, at an annual interest rate of 10%); 2. The defendant to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense:

1. The liability for culpa in contrahendo exists only during the formation of the contract. The fifteen commercial housing sale contracts involved in this case and the agreement on debt settlement through property are true and represent the genuine intention of both parties, and have been fully performed. The defendant has no culpa in contrahendo. 2. The defendant did not engage in the negligent conduct alleged by the plaintiffs. Regarding the nature of the commercial housing sale contract, the defendant is only obliged to inform the other party of the main terms concerning the property's location, area, quality, and whether there are any disputes over ownership. The plaintiffs, when signing the commercial housing sale contract, had already been informed that the property was subject to a third-party lease and acknowledged the lease. As for the lessee's performance capability claimed by the plaintiffs, it falls within the plaintiffs' scope of review. 3. Rent is a statutory fruit. After the ownership transfer, the obligation to collect rent transfers to the new owner. 4. When the plaintiffs and the defendant signed the commercial housing sale contract on March 29, 2013, the defendant had already lawfully disclosed to the plaintiffs the existence of a prior lease contract for the property, and the plaintiffs confirmed and signed the lease contract as an attachment. On the following day, the defendant timely notified the lessee of the transfer. Throughout the entire commercial housing sale contract, the defendant did not commit any breach of contract. 5. The relationship between the plaintiffs and the defendant is a commercial housing sale relationship. The rent and related interest claimed by the plaintiffs are based on statutory succession. The plaintiffs passively exercised their rights and voluntarily waived their right of recourse against the lessee, Hefei Junyue Company. The ultimate loss suffered by the plaintiffs was caused by their passive exercise of rights. The plaintiffs' demand that the defendant bear losses such as rent has no legal basis.

Facts Found by the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province at First Instance:

In July 2012, Tang Xuefu, Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch, and Hefei Jianxin Company entered into a "Supplementary Agreement on Debt Settlement through Property" regarding the project funds owed by Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch to Tang Xuefu. The agreement confirmed that Hefei Jianxin Company owed Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch project funds of RMB 34,820,000. The agreement also stipulated that Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch would purchase properties developed by Hefei Jianxin Company, located at Units 113-118, 213-217, 313-317, 413-415, and 417, Block B, Haidun Mansion Commercial Street, Taihu Road, Hefei (total area 2,543.13 square meters, total price RMB 31,297,281), and transfer them to Tang Xuefu, with the purchase price to be offset against the project funds payable by Hefei Jianxin Company to Greenfield Construction Hefei Branch. On March 29, 2013, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua signed fifteen "Commercial Housing Sale Contracts" with Hefei Jianxin Company, under which Hefei Jianxin Company agreed to sell the subject properties to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. On the supplementary agreement column of the last page of each contract, an employee of Hefei Jianxin Company wrote: "The client has been informed that the property has been leased and agrees that the original lease contract shall remain in effect. Original lease contract number: HAID08001(TJ)."

On March 5, 2013, the plaintiffs Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua sent a reminder letter to the defendant Hefei Jianxin Company, demanding the payment of rent of RMB 1,404,396 and late fees of RMB 140,439. On April 10, 2013, Hefei Jianxin Company transferred RMB 1,258,712 to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua as rent for eight months (from August 1, 2012, to March 31, 2013). On April 23, 2013, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, through a law firm, again sent a letter to Hefei Jianxin Company demanding rent, but Hefei Jianxin Company refused to pay.

On June 4, 2013, the plaintiffs Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua completed the registration of ownership of the above properties.

On July 23, 2013, Hefei Jianxin Company filed a lawsuit with the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, against Hefei Junyue Company, seeking an order that Hefei Junyue Company pay the overdue rent of RMB 1,404,396 (including the rent of RMB 1,258,712 previously advanced by Hefei Jianxin Company) and liquidated damages, but did not seek rescission of the lease contract. At the same time, Hefei Jianxin Company applied to the court for preservation of the equipment in Hefei Junyue Company's business premises. On March 6, 2014, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua filed a lawsuit with the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, against Hefei Jianxin Company and Hefei Junyue Company, seeking an order that Hefei Junyue Company pay overdue rent of RMB 2,039,114.88 and liquidated damages of RMB 20,391.15. On October 10, 2014, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua applied to the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, to withdraw the lawsuit, and the application was granted.

Additionally, it was found that: On March 19, 2008, Hefei Jianxin Company (Party A) and Hefei Junyue Company (Party B) entered into a "Lease Contract" regarding the properties in question. Party A was to deliver the properties to Party B before April 1, 2008, and the lease term was from April 1, 2008, to March 31, 2018. After the contract was signed, Hefei Junyue Company paid a deposit and leased the properties for operating a restaurant and KTV business. During the term, Hefei Junyue Company paid part of the rent, but was in arrears for the rent of March 2012 and the period from August 2012 to March 31, 2013.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance:

*Regarding the cause of action:* The subject of this case is not the subject matter of the sale contract itself, nor the rights and obligations under the lease contract, but whether there is a causal relationship between the sale and the infringement of lease rights. The plaintiffs, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, filed the lawsuit based on the defendant Hefei Jianxin Company's liability for culpa in contrahendo. Therefore, the dispute in this case is not about the commercial attributes of the transacted properties, such as area and structure, but about functions derivative of the transaction subject matter. A seller of goods not only bears obligations regarding the quality of the subject matter itself but also certain ancillary obligations. When delivering the subject matter, the seller must ensure the property is free from defects and that the buyer can acquire the subject matter and properly exercise the rights attaching to it as agreed. If the seller delivers a defective subject matter, causing loss to the buyer, it constitutes defective performance. Liability for guarantee against defects is a type of liability for guarantee against defects in the goods, a special form of liability for breach of contract, namely, the liability the seller bears for violating its guarantee obligation when the goods sold have defects. Therefore, the cause of action in this case should be determined as a dispute over liability for guarantee against defects in performance.

*Regarding the responsibility of the defendant Hefei Jianxin Company:* When delivering the subject matter, Hefei Jianxin Company should ensure that the functions and powers of the property are free from defects and assist Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua in completing the actual delivery or other appropriate handover procedures. In this case, on the one hand, Hefei Jianxin Company was transacting the sale of the property with Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua; on the other hand, it was pursuing rent from Hefei Junyue Company through litigation. However, Hefei Jianxin Company deliberately concealed this important fact and used the method of advancing rent to cover it up, indicating subjective intent, with the result that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were unaware of the imminent risks when purchasing the property. Since the properties in question are commercial shops, their purchase purpose is to obtain income through leasing. Therefore, the root cause of the actual risks subsequently faced by Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua is the defect in the subject matter delivered by Hefei Jianxin Company. Hefei Jianxin Company's conduct in this case constitutes defective performance and shall bear liability for guarantee against defects in performance according to law.

Pursuant to Article 92 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which provides: "After the termination of rights and obligations under a contract, the parties shall perform the obligations of notification, assistance, confidentiality, etc., in accordance with the principle of good faith and in light of the trade practice," the defendant Hefei Jianxin Company failed to provide evidence that it had, after signing the contract, used appropriate means to notify the lessee Hefei Junyue Company of the transfer of ownership of the property, nor did it handle any procedures for the alteration of the lease relationship, nor did it make appropriate arrangements regarding the sealing of the equipment, resulting in the plaintiffs Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua being unable to claim rent as a lessor or to actually use the property as an owner. Hefei Jianxin Company's failure to timely perform its post-contractual obligations also constitutes improper performance of the contract and shall bear liability for damages.

*Regarding the plaintiffs' voluntary withdrawal of the lawsuit:* Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua filed a lawsuit on March 6, 2014, against Hefei Jianxin Company and Hefei Junyue Company to recover rent, indicating that at that time they had become aware that Hefei Junyue Company was the lessee of the property. However, the plaintiffs' voluntary withdrawal of the lawsuit cannot be automatically deemed as a waiver of their substantive rights. Given the complex background of the transaction, even if Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua had not withdrawn the lawsuit, under the circumstances where the property was sealed and still under court enforcement, they could not recover or actually possess the property, nor could they realize the real rights of possession, use, and enjoyment of proceeds. Therefore, the loss of rent during this period is also a loss arising from the breach of contractual obligations.

*Regarding the calculation and apportionment of losses:* The losses claimed by the plaintiffs Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua are in the form of rent, but in substance, they are losses caused by the defendant Hefei Jianxin Company's fault in preventing the collection of rent. It is not inappropriate for Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua to use the rent standard as the method for calculating the loss. The calculation period for this loss should be from April 1, 2013, to the date of actual delivery of the property, i.e., October 11, 2015. For the above rent loss, the parties shall bear responsibility in proportion to their respective degrees of fault. The fault of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua lies in: As persons with full capacity for civil conduct, they should have exercised due diligence when signing the contract. Their failure to do so results in their bearing a certain degree of responsibility. The fault of Hefei Jianxin Company has three aspects: 1. When signing the "Commercial Housing Sale Contract," it concealed the important fact that the lessee was in arrears with rent, violating its pre-contractual obligations. 2. After signing the sale contract, it failed to timely deliver the lease contract to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, failed to timely notify the lessee of the change in ownership of the property, and failed to assist Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua in completing the property handover procedures, including altering the lease relationship or timely notifying the lessee of the change in ownership, thereby violating its post-contractual obligations. 3. Hefei Jianxin Company sued Hefei Junyue Company only for rent payment but did not seek rescission of the lease contract, and it applied for property preservation to seal the items inside the property, objectively preventing Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua from recovering and using the property. In this regard, Hefei Jianxin Company bears some fault. Based on the respective degrees of fault between the plaintiffs and Hefei Jianxin Company, the court of first instance determined that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua shall bear 30% of the responsibility and Hefei Jianxin Company shall bear 70% of the responsibility. The rent loss for the subject property from April 1, 2013, to October 11, 2015, amounts to RMB 5,503,244.84. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua bear 30%, i.e., RMB 1,650,973, and Hefei Jianxin Company bears 70%, i.e., RMB 3,852,271. After fulfilling the liability for guarantee against defects, Hefei Jianxin Company has the right to seek recourse against Hefei Junyue Company.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 42, 60, and 92 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, rendered a judgment on May 16, 2016:

1. Hefei Jianxin Company shall pay Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua rent loss of RMB 3,852,271 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;
2. After fulfilling the liability determined in item 1 above, Hefei Jianxin Company has the right to seek recourse against Hefei Junyue Company;
3. All other claims of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua are dismissed.

Tang Xuefu, Pang Hua, and Hefei Jianxin Company were all dissatisfied and appealed to the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province.

Appeal by Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua:

Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua argued that they suffered losses due to Hefei Jianxin Company's material fraudulent concealment during the transaction. The cause is entirely due to Hefei Jianxin Company's violation of the principle of good faith in civil activities. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua bear no fault, and full responsibility should be borne by Hefei Jianxin Company. The losses suffered by Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua include not only the direct rent loss but also the corresponding interest loss resulting from the failure to collect rent in a timely manner. Hefei Jianxin Company should compensate for these losses. They requested the court of second instance to: set aside the first-instance judgment and amend it to order Hefei Jianxin Company to compensate Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua for rent loss of RMB 5,503,244.84 and corresponding interest.

Response by Hefei Jianxin Company:

Hefei Jianxin Company argued that when Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua signed the contracts in question, they were fully aware of the existence of the lease contract. Pursuant to the principle that "sale does not break lease," Hefei Jianxin Company was not required to arrange for the other party to sign a new lease contract with the lessee. After the commercial housing sale contract was signed and the ownership transfer was completed, the risk of inability to collect rent was borne by Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Hefei Jianxin Company bears no guarantee liability for the rent. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua have the right to claim rent from the original lessee. The consequences of their withdrawing the lawsuit against Hefei Junyue Company and waiving their right to rent should be borne by themselves. Hefei Jianxin Company lawfully exercised its rights against Hefei Junyue Company after advancing the rent, and the sealing of Hefei Junyue Company's equipment was legally justified and did not harm the actual interests of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

Hefei Jianxin Company appealed, arguing: 1. Hefei Jianxin Company did not maliciously conceal any information; Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were aware of the leasing of the property. Informing the buyers of the lessee's ability to perform does not constitute a pre-contractual obligation of Hefei Jianxin Company. According to the Contract Law, the Judicial Interpretation of the Contract Law on Sales Contracts, the Judicial Interpretation on the Sale of Commodity Houses, and trade practices, the seller's pre-contractual disclosure obligations in the formation of a commodity house sales contract do not include the lessee's ability to perform. The "House Sales Contract" signed between Hefei Jianxin Company and Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua clearly stipulated the basic conditions of the house, the price, the handling of discrepancies, the delivery date, the registration of property rights, and related liability for breach of contract. Hefei Jianxin Company has strictly fulfilled its contractual and statutory obligations and there is no defective performance. 2. Hefei Jianxin Company fully performed its assistance obligations, promptly delivered the lease contract to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, assisted them in registering the property rights, and promptly notified the lessee of the change in property ownership. 3. Hefei Junyue Company owed rent to Hefei Jianxin Company before the house was sold. Hefei Jianxin Company has the right to demand that Hefei Junyue Company pay the rent due before the change of property ownership and to apply for compulsory enforcement. Given that at the time Hefei Jianxin Company filed the lawsuit, the property rights to the house in question had already been transferred and the lessor of the house had changed to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, Hefei Jianxin Company could not claim to terminate the original "House Lease Contract". 4. The "Commodity House Sales Contract" signed between Hefei Jianxin Company and Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua clearly stipulated the price of the house. This price only included the value of the house itself and did not include the value of prospective gains such as rent. After Hefei Jianxin Company sold the house, the responsibility for leasing the house was transferred. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua should bear the commercial risks associated with the leasing transaction, and losses due to rent and interest do not fall within the scope of compensable losses in this case. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were negligent in exercising their rights and voluntarily abandoned their rights, causing the losses from rent and interest in this case. Such losses should not be compensated by Hefei Jianxin Company. Hefei Jianxin Company requested the court of second instance to: set aside the judgment of first instance and enter a judgment dismissing all claims of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua responded, arguing: 1. Hefei Jianxin Company's performance was defective, and it should bear corresponding liability for warranty against defects in performance. Although Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua knew that the house in question had been leased before the sale, Hefei Jianxin Company deliberately concealed the material fact that the lessee, Hefei Junyue Company, lacked the ability to perform. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were unaware of the lessee's performance status. Due to its dominant position in the transaction, Hefei Jianxin Company did not hand over the "House Lease Contract" to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua when signing the "Commodity House Sales Contract". Instead, Hefei Jianxin Company noted on the signing page of the contract: "The customer is aware that the property has been leased and undertakes that the original lease contract shall remain in effect." For a considerable period after signing the "Commodity House Sales Contract", Hefei Jianxin Company still did not deliver the "House Lease Contract" to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua repeatedly requested Hefei Jianxin Company to perform its obligations, including notifying the lessee of the change in property rights and handing over the "House Lease Contract", but Hefei Jianxin Company delayed and refused to do so. It was not until the end of 2013 that Hefei Jianxin Company finally delivered the "House Lease Contract" to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Although Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were aware at the time of the transaction that the property was leased and the identity of the lessee, they did not know that the lessee had already fallen into a state of inability to perform. Hefei Jianxin Company deliberately concealed the lessee's inability to perform during the formation and performance of the sales contract, creating a significant risk for Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. 2. The lessee Hefei Junyue Company's ability to perform falls within the pre-contractual obligations that Hefei Jianxin Company must fulfill. According to the principle of "sale does not break a lease," Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua cannot assert their ownership of the house to defeat the leasehold right of the lessee, Hefei Junyue Company. The house in question is a commercial shop. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua purchased it with a view to the income that could be generated from leasing. However, during the formation of the "Commodity House Sales Contract", Hefei Jianxin Company did not inform Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua of the fact that the lessee could not perform, thereby causing Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua to bear an undue risk. 3. Hefei Jianxin Company's incomplete performance of its contractual obligations constitutes defective performance. According to the law, the seller bears a warranty against defects in title. The seller must ensure that the sold property is free from defects in title and that the functions and attributes of the property are free from defects. The house in question is a commercial shop. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua purchased it for the purpose of generating income through leasing. The actual risk faced by Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua after purchasing the house originates from the defect in the house delivered by Hefei Jianxin Company. Hefei Jianxin Company's performance is defective, and it should bear liability for warranty against defects in performance. 4. Hefei Jianxin Company objectively caused Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua to be unable to recover and use the house. Before the sale of the house in question (March 29, 2013), the lessee Hefei Junyue Company had already failed to pay rent for nine months. However, Hefei Jianxin Company did not exercise its right to terminate the contract before the sale, nor did it recover the house and then sell it to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Shortly after the transfer of the house, Hefei Jianxin Company sued Hefei Junyue Company and applied for the seizure of the business equipment inside the house. As a result, while the equipment inside the house was legally seized and during the period of compulsory enforcement, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua could not recover or actually possess the house, nor could they realize the property rights of possession, use, and enjoyment. Hefei Jianxin Company's act of preserving property and applying for seizure violated its contractual obligations, rendering the delivered subject matter defective. 5. After purchasing the house in question, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua repeatedly negotiated with Hefei Junyue Company to demand payment of the overdue rent. Hefei Junyue Company refused to pay rent on the grounds that Hefei Jianxin Company had not notified it of the change in the lease relationship and that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were not parties to the lease contract. After Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua sued Hefei Junyue Company in court, their subsequent withdrawal of the lawsuit was their right. This act did not mean that they abandoned their substantive rights, nor was it a failure to diligently exercise their rights.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province held in the second instance:

According to Article 39 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, an owner of a real or movable property is entitled to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of his or her property in accordance with the law. In law, the owner may separate the above rights from ownership for different entities to enjoy and exercise in accordance with the law. Leasing the property to a lessee is a typical form of separating the rights of possession and use for the lessee to actually enjoy and exercise. When the owner sells the leased property to a buyer, in order to maintain normal transaction order, Article 229 of the Contract Law provides that a change in the ownership of the leased property during the lease term shall not affect the validity of the lease contract. This provision means that the original lease contract between the seller and the lessee does not terminate due to the change in ownership; it remains binding on the buyer. After acquiring ownership, the buyer replaces the seller as the lessor in the lease contract and succeeds to the seller's rights and obligations under the original lease contract. In this case, after becoming the owner of the property in question, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua have the right to claim against the lessee Hefei Junyue Company under the original lease contract for the rights enjoyed by the lessor, and also assume the burden of the partial separation of the property rights from ownership, which had already been lawfully possessed and used by Hefei Junyue Company under the lease contract. The original lessor, Hefei Jianxin Company, no longer has the rights and obligations of the lessor.

Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua stated in the second instance that the content "The customer is aware that the property has been leased and undertakes that the original lease shall remain in effect" in all the commodity house sales contracts signed on March 29, 2013, was written by Tang Xuefu himself, and that he knew Hefei Junyue Company was the lessee of the property in question. The court of second instance held that during the formation of a sales contract for a leased property, the buyer can independently judge and decide whether to enter into the house sales contract with the seller based on the content of the lease contract and the lessee's performance. In the absence of fraudulent conduct such as intentional concealment of facts or misrepresentation, or other dishonest conduct by Hefei Jianxin Company, the risk to the lessor arising from Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's failure to request specific information about the lease from Hefei Jianxin Company or to actively verify and examine the relevant materials should be borne by themselves. Hefei Junyue Company, based on the house lease contract with Hefei Jianxin Company, has the right to lawfully possess and use the leased property. After Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua became the owners of the leased property, Hefei Junyue Company's right is not affected by the change in ownership. In other words, Hefei Jianxin Company is legally unable and not required to make a direct handover of possession and use of the property in the usual sense to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. It should be understood that Hefei Jianxin Company has indirectly completed the handover by delivering the property to Hefei Junyue Company, the lessee under the contract of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

The ownership of the property in question was registered in the names of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua on June 4, 2013. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua should have been entitled to collect rent from that date. However, they had already collected rent paid on their behalf by Hefei Jianxin Company before that time. In this regard, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua stated that it was a mutual agreement that after July 2012, they would collect the rent. Hefei Jianxin Company stated that because this case involved using the property to offset a previous debt, and both parties clearly understood that the property was subject to an existing lease contract, and that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua could not actually possess or need to actually possess the property during the lease term, the parties considered that upon signing the debt offset agreement, the property was deemed to have been actually delivered to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. The house sales contract did not stipulate a delivery date for the property. The court of second instance held that, based on the above rent payments and the statements of the parties, at least before April 10, 2013, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua knew that they had the right to collect rent from the lessee Hefei Junyue Company. They had also sued Hefei Junyue Company in March 2014 to assert this right. Therefore, the responsibility for their current inability to realize rent income lies entirely with themselves and is unrelated to Hefei Jianxin Company.

One of the core reasons Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua sought to impose liability on Hefei Jianxin Company in this case is that the company concealed the material fact that Hefei Junyue Company was in arrears on rent and created the illusion of normal performance of the lease contract by making advance rent payments, thereby causing them to be unable to realize the right to rent income for a long period after purchasing the property. However, as previously discussed: First, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua failed to provide any evidence in this case proving that Hefei Jianxin Company concealed the fact that Hefei Junyue Company was in arrears on rent before the change of ownership of the property. Even if Hefei Junyue Company was objectively in arrears on rent, Hefei Jianxin Company advanced the rent payments that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were entitled to, so there is no resulting loss to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Second, after not receiving rent after April 1, 2013, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua could have, based on their agreement with Hefei Jianxin Company, demanded that Hefei Junyue Company pay the overdue rent. Alternatively, after June 4, 2013, as owners of the property, they could have demanded that Hefei Junyue Company pay the overdue rent, or they could have protected their rights in a timely manner by terminating the lease contract. However, they did not actively take legal action; they only sued Hefei Jianxin Company and Hefei Junyue Company in March 2014 and eventually withdrew the lawsuit. Clearly, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's claim that Hefei Jianxin Company bears legal liability for their loss of rent income is untenable. Third, after the change of ownership of the leased property, the seller can notify the lessee, and the buyer can also notify the lessee. The buyer can either negotiate with the lessee to re-sign a house lease contract or continue to perform under the original lease contract without re-signing. Hefei Jianxin Company therefore is not at fault in this regard. Fourth, whether Hefei Jianxin Company, as the original lessor, sued the lessee Hefei Junyue Company for overdue rent during the performance of the lease contract, or sought to recover the rent it had advanced on behalf of Hefei Junyue Company to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, these are rights it enjoys under the law. Its application to the court to preserve the property of Hefei Junyue Company is also a right it enjoys under the law to protect its own interests. This does not constitute a wrongful infringement of the legitimate rights and interests of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

In conclusion, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, in accordance with subparagraph (2) of Article 170(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a judgment on October 28, 2016:

1. Set aside the civil judgment of the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei, Anhui Province (2016) Wan 0111 Min Chu No. 192;

2. Dismiss the claims of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, dissatisfied, applied to the Anhui High People's Court for retrial, arguing: The court of second instance unreasonably allocated the burden of proof between Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua and Hefei Jianxin Company, making findings favorable to Hefei Jianxin Company and unfavorable to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. The basic facts confirmed lacked evidentiary support and constituted errors in fact-finding. Specifically: 1. Before the "Debt Offset Supplementary Agreement" was signed, the lessee of the property in question, Hefei Junyue Company, had already failed to pay one month's rent. Hefei Jianxin Company knew that the rent would be difficult to collect but did not inform Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. Therefore, the court of second instance erred in finding that Hefei Jianxin Company did not intentionally conceal facts or fabricate circumstances, leading Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua to mistakenly believe that the rent from the property in question was substantial and to agree to the debt-for-property arrangement. 2. When the lessee was in serious breach, Hefei Jianxin Company could have terminated the contract and recovered the property. However, it only sent a demand letter and did not remove the encumbrance on the property's rights before signing the "Commodity House Sales Contract," thereby shifting the risk of being unable to collect rent to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. The court of second instance erred in finding that the responsibility for Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's inability to collect rent lay with themselves and was unrelated to Hefei Jianxin Company. 3. After signing the "Commodity House Sales Contract" for the property in question but before the property rights were transferred into the names of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, Hefei Jianxin Company concealed the fact that the lessee had not paid rent for eight months by advancing rent payments; after the property rights were transferred, Hefei Jianxin Company sued the lessee for rent and applied for the seizure of the property inside the house, which objectively hindered Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua from recovering the house. The court of second instance erred in finding that Hefei Jianxin Company's application for preservation of the lessee's property did not constitute harm to the legitimate rights and interests of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua. 4. When transferring the property in question, Hefei Jianxin Company did not inform the lessee of its preemptive right to purchase, causing the lessee to refuse to recognize Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua as the lessor on the grounds that it was unaware the property was being sold, and therefore refused to pay rent. As for Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua suing the lessee and then withdrawing the lawsuit, this was a disposition of their own rights and does not affect their substantive right to claim rent from the lessee. The court of second instance erred in finding that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua failed to act actively in accordance with the law when their rights were harmed. Pursuant to subparagraphs (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua requested the Anhui High People's Court to: set aside the civil judgment of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province (2016) Wan 01 Min Zhong No. 3976, and enter a judgment in favor of the claims of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua.

The Anhui High People's Court, upon review, held:

Because Hefei Jianxin Company owed project payments, it transferred the property in question to Tang Hua to offset the debt; the purchase price was to be deducted from the project payments owed by Hefei Jianxin Company. The substance of the agreement between the parties is that one party delivered the property, and the other party used the outstanding project payments owed by the former to offset the purchase price. Therefore, the nature of the "Debt Offset Supplementary Agreement" is a house sales contract. Subsequently, the parties signed fifteen "Commodity House Sales Contracts" to confirm the fact of the house sale. Article 132(1) of the Contract Law provides that the subject matter of a sale shall belong to the seller or be under the seller's authority to dispose of. Article 148 provides that if the quality of the subject matter does not meet the requirements, making it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract, the buyer may reject the subject matter or terminate the contract. If the buyer rejects the subject matter or terminates the contract, the risk of damage or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the seller. From the above legal provisions, it is clear that in a sales contract, the seller has an obligation to warrant title and quality of the subject matter. In this case, the seller Hefei Jianxin Company bears the warranty liability for the ownership and quality of the house. As to this part—that Hefei Jianxin Company lawfully held the ownership of the property in question and that the quality of the house met the delivery standards—the parties did not dispute. The root of the dispute in this case is that the property transferred was one that Hefei Jianxin Company had leased. Given that the lessee was in arrears on rent, whether Hefei Jianxin Company's transfer of the property harmed the interests of the buyers Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, and whether it should compensate them for the loss of rent. In this regard, the Anhui High People's Court held that, based on the facts and evidence in this case, Hefei Jianxin Company should not bear liability for compensating the loss of rent. The reasons are as follows:

1. Article 229 of the Contract Law provides that a change in the ownership of the leased property during the lease term shall not affect the validity of the lease contract. Accordingly, the ownership of the leased property may be transferred during the lease term; after the transfer of ownership, the original lease contract remains valid. That is, if a buyer purchases a property that is leased, they must be bound by the original lease contract. In this case, when the parties signed the sales contract, they noted in the supplementary agreement column: "The customer is aware that the property has been leased and undertakes that the original lease contract shall remain in effect. Original lease contract number: HAID08001(TJ)". Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua also acknowledged in the second instance that they knew the property was leased. Based on the above content in the contract, the admission of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua, and their conduct in agreeing to purchase the property, it can be determined that Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were willing to be bound by the lease contract.

2. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua applied for retrial, arguing that Hefei Jianxin Company deliberately concealed the fact that the lessee did not pay rent on time, causing them to be unaware of this potential risk when purchasing the property in question. In this regard, the Anhui High People's Court held that a lessee's failure to pay rent on time in a lease contract is not an isolated occurrence. As a lessor, one should anticipate such a situation. Therefore, lease contract terms usually stipulate the rights the lessor may enjoy and the lessee's liability for breach if the lessee fails to pay rent on time. Thus, for a lessor, the inability to collect rent on time falls within the category of market risk. By agreeing to be bound by the lease contract, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua also had to assume such commercial risks.

III. Whether Hefei Jianxin Company intentionally concealed the fact that rent had not been collected.
Hefei Jianxin Company entered into a lease contract with the lessee Junyue Company in 2008, and signed the *Supplemental Agreement for Property Transfer* with Tang Xuefu and others in July 2012. Although the property ownership registration for the involved premises was completed in June 2013, in light of the parties' performance of the agreement, the rent for the involved premises began to be delivered to Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua as early as August 2012. At that time, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua were not the owners of the premises and had no right to directly collect the rent from the lessee. Therefore, it was reasonable for Hefei Jianxin Company to pay Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua the rent from August 2012 to March 2013. The fact that Hefei Jianxin Company advanced the rent on behalf of the lessee does not, by itself, prove that Hefei Jianxin Company had the subjective intent to deliberately conceal from Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua the lessee's overdue rent.

IV. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua have statutory legal remedies for the lessee's overdue rent.
In June 2013, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua obtained the ownership certificates for the involved premises and became the owners thereof. From the moment they received the ownership certificates, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua acquired the legal right to collect rent for the involved premises. This right is both a contractual right and a statutory right. As the assignees of the involved premises, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua directly succeeded to the rights that the original owner held over the premises. If the lessee failed to pay rent, Tang and Pang could have pursued the matter in accordance with the lease contract. Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua did file a lawsuit against the lessee in March 2014 demanding payment of rent, but subsequently withdrew the lawsuit. Indeed, withdrawing the lawsuit against the lessee was their statutory right; however, at the same time, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua must also bear the legal consequences arising from their waiver of that right. Moreover, as Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua argued in their retrial application, if the lessee refused to pay rent on the ground that its preemptive purchase right had been infringed, then that issue should have been clarified and the dispute resolved through trial by the People's Court. They could not simply transfer the lessee's liability for non-payment of rent directly to Hefei Jianxin Company. Consequently, after withdrawing their lawsuit against the lessee for rent payment, Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's claim to hold Hefei Jianxin Company liable for compensation is manifestly difficult to sustain.

V. Hefei Jianxin Company's lawsuit against the lessee does not constitute an infringement of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's rights.
In July 2013, Hefei Jianxin Company filed a lawsuit against the lessee demanding payment of overdue rent. This lawsuit was a legitimate method for Hefei Jianxin Company to use legal means to resolve the dispute and protect its own lawful rights and interests in the face of the lessee's breach of contract. During the trial phase, Hefei Jianxin Company lawfully applied to the People's Court to seize the lessee's property located within the involved premises, which complied with legal provisions. There is no direct causal relationship between Hefei Jianxin Company's lawsuit against the lessee and whether Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua could obtain rent from the lessee. Furthermore, from a legal perspective, it is impermissible to require Hefei Jianxin Company, absent any statutory or contractual obligation, to waive its own legally protected rights merely to ensure the exercise of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua's rights.

In summary, the Anhui High People's Court, pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following ruling on April 13, 2018:

The retrial application of Tang Xuefu and Pang Hua is rejected.
